ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Bronchial asthma: 1

A young adult has recurrent wheeze and chest tightness that vary over time. Spirometry during symptoms shows obstruction that improves substantially after bronchodilator treatment. Which physiological feature most strongly supports asthma in this presentation?

  1. Type 2 airway inflammation
  2. Trigger-associated worsening of airway narrowing
  3. Bronchial hyperresponsiveness
  4. Variable expiratory airflow limitation
  5. Repeat objective testing when symptomatic or use an appropriate variability test
Answer and explanation

Variable expiratory airflow limitation

Episodic symptoms plus demonstrably variable expiratory airflow support asthma; variability is a defining diagnostic feature.

Option explanations

Variable expiratory airflow limitation: Episodic symptoms plus demonstrably variable expiratory airflow support asthma; variability is a defining diagnostic feature.

Repeat objective testing when symptomatic or use an appropriate variability test: Normal spirometry between episodes does not exclude asthma; diagnostic confirmation may require repeated or alternative testing. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Type 2 airway inflammation: Eosinophilic inflammation is a common asthma phenotype, involving pathways such as IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13; not all asthma is eosinophilic. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Trigger-associated worsening of airway narrowing: Viral infections, allergens and irritants can provoke symptoms in susceptible airways without each episode implying bacterial pneumonia. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Bronchial hyperresponsiveness: Excessive airway narrowing to a stimulus is characteristic of hyperresponsive airways, although challenge results require clinical interpretation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
